answer: One workable design: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because comet only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, glacier is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any pigment approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
